build_rules: No line carries the 'Native integration' line type. Adobe does not use that word for ChatGPT or Claude on the pages cited (on the GenStudio page it uses it for Coworker only). The lines are drawn plain, like 138 of the tool's 162 connections today.

A play offers ChatGPT and Claude whenever a product on its canvas connects to them. At the start that is the Adobe Coworker play, Brand Visibility + Customer Journey Analytics and Create your own play. Once the ranked Add product list is in, adding such a product to any other play brings the two entries with it.

The lines to AEM Sites and the service 'AEM content work in ChatGPT or Claude' need AEM Sites added as its own product. They must not appear when the tool counts AEM Sites as on the canvas only because Edge Delivery Services is there with AEM authoring: Adobe's page covers AEM as a Cloud Service and does not mention Edge Delivery Services. The build needs a check for this.
Overlap review: add the pairs listed under each new service's 'overlaps' (canvas OVERLAP and the SOW steps' OVERLAPS), so the statement of work asks how the two differ when both are on.
Each new service needs its basis and three sizes in the SOW steps (given here as basis and bands) and an RFI write-up of its own: seven new write-ups.

RFI Builder: ChatGPT and Claude become named outside systems with the same guard Figma got on Nov 17. 'Do you use ChatGPT or Claude in delivering services?' stays the partner's own answer, 'Our designers and analysts all use ChatGPT' matches nothing, and 'show up in ChatGPT' stays with Brand Visibility. Each needs a check.
The ranked Add product list goes in first (it is built and waiting for Adam). This build goes on top of it, and its pictures are retaken on the real screens before anything is saved.
No release label, date, caveat or note about what is coming or left out, anywhere in the tool (Adam, Nov 18).
Real limits stay inside the how sentence (look only, roles, what the assistant cannot read); no new card section.
